messages:
sophia: FYI ran the onboarding qual for magnet-16b int4v3 with an extended context replay (50k tokens) and saw a deterministic divergence in model outputs after ~20,480 tokens compared to the oracle replay baseline. checksum drift + token alignment mismatch. attaching short logs below.

ben: ack. can you paste the exact run command and the smallest repro? also which kv_prefill_mode?

sophia: repro command:
```
./onboard.sh --model magnet-16b --quant int4v3 --context 51200 --prefill-mode oracle-replay --seed 42 --debug-kv=1
```
Log snippet:
```
[2026-03-21 11:12:05] prefill.len=51200 prefill.mode=oracle-replay
[2026-03-21 11:13:27] kv.checksum=0x7a3b12ff (oracle)
[2026-03-21 11:13:27] kv.checksum=0x7a3b12ad (live)  <-- divergence at token 20480
```
I also tried `--prefill-mode inflight-catchup` and it moves the divergence point slightly but doesn't eliminate it.

kai: interesting. any pattern to the tokens at the boundary (newline runs, long repeated tokens)? could be rotary phase wrap + quantized rounding.

sophia: boundary looks like a long code block + lots of backticks. not a simple repeated token case. I instrumented ropestate and saw phase offsets diverging by a few microsteps after the boundary.

mira: did you run with the CLOCK_WRAP_FIX branch? we had a similar symptom when high-context prefill hit the phase rescale path under int4 quantization. try `ROPE_SCALE_MODE=continuous` vs `discrete` to see if phase interpolation is the culprit.

ben: also try running with `KV_PREFILL_STRIDE=4096` smaller stride to force more frequent kv writes; could hide an off-by-one memory copy.

sophia: will run both. launching two CI jobs now. @infra-bot can you link the runs when they start?

infra-bot: CI job started: https://ci.redwood/eng-ml/17200 (oracle-replay + CLOCK_WRAP_FIX test)
infra-bot: CI job started: https://ci.redwood/eng-ml/17201 (inflight-catchup + KV_PREFILL_STRIDE=4096)

ben: thanks. if both fail, next step is to try a pure FP16 build (no int4 kernels) to confirm quant kernel is involved. if fp16 matches oracle, then we know where to bisect.

mira: one more thought — the divergence point aligning near 20,480 smells like a window-shrink boundary (2^11 * 10). could be a tiled-KV flush that doesn't update the rotary phase accumulator consistently across shards. check cross-shard handshake logs (`kvsync.*`).

sophia: noted. I'll collect `kvsync.*` and `ropestate.*` traces and post results here when the CI jobs finish. ETA ~40m.

ben: cool. if this reproduces locally, let's make a minimal unit test that runs the 21k token prefix and asserts checksum equality between oracle and inflight. that'll speed bisecting.

sophia: agreed. adding to my todo. will update with links and diffs. :mag:
